Robert Haldane
ROB-urt HAWL-dayn
proper noun (person)
Scottish Reformed layman, philanthropist, and theologian (1764-1842), author of an Exposition of the Epistle to the Romans and catalyst of the Geneva revival.

📖 Biblical Definition

Robert Haldane was a wealthy Scottish landowner who, converted to a vital evangelical faith, devoted his fortune and his energies to the spread of the gospel, and became, with his brother James, a leading figure of revival in Scotland and beyond. Selling his estate to fund missions and gospel work, he supported preachers, founded churches, and labored for the conversion of the lost. His most famous and far-reaching service came during a visit to Geneva and Montauban, where he gathered theological students — many of them spiritually dead in the rationalism of the day — and taught them through the Epistle to the Romans verse by verse. Under that teaching a number were soundly converted, including men like Merle d'Aubigné, César Malan, and Frédéric Monod, who became leaders of the evangelical "Réveil" (Awakening) across French-speaking Europe. Out of those studies came Haldane's massive Exposition of the Epistle to the Romans, a rich and thorough commentary on the doctrines of grace. Haldane stands in the dictionary as the layman who sparked the Geneva revival, who proved that the patient teaching of the Epistle to the Romans can raise the spiritually dead, and whose stewardship of wealth and gifts for the gospel is a pattern of consecrated means.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

Scottish Reformed layman and theologian (1764-1842), author of an Exposition of Romans; who sold his estate for the gospel and, by teaching Romans to Geneva students, sparked the evangelical "Réveil" across French-speaking Europe.

ROBERT HALDANE, proper noun. Scottish Reformed layman and theologian (1764-1842).

A wealthy landowner converted to vital evangelical faith.

Sold his estate and gave his fortune to the spread of the gospel.

Taught Romans to Geneva students, sparking the evangelical "Réveil."

Author of a massive Exposition of the Epistle to the Romans.

📖 Key Scripture

Rom 1:16 — "For I am not ashamed of the gospel of Christ: for it is the power of God unto salvation to every one that believeth; to the Jew first, and also to the Greek."

Rom 1:17 — "For therein is the righteousness of God revealed from faith to faith: as it is written, The just shall live by faith."

2 Cor 9:7 — "...for God loveth a cheerful giver."

1 Tim 6:18 — "That they do good, that they be rich in good works, ready to distribute, willing to communicate;"

⚠️ Modern Corruption

Haldane's life honors the recovery of Romans as the power of God to raise the spiritually dead, and of the consecrated stewardship of wealth for the gospel, against a dead rationalism and a hoarding of means.

expand to see more

Rationalism correction. The Geneva students Haldane taught had been schooled in a rationalism that emptied the gospel of its power. By simply opening the Epistle to the Romans, Haldane saw the dead made alive. The dictionary holds that the gospel of Romans is "the power of God unto salvation" (Rom 1:16); no human academy or system can substitute for the plain teaching of the Word, which alone raises the spiritually dead and revives the church.

This entry faces little postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is the stewardship of wealth and gifts for the kingdom. Haldane sold his estate and poured his fortune into gospel work, a cheerful giver (2 Cor 9:7) rich in good works (1 Tim 6:18). The dictionary commends his example against a hoarding spirit: what God entrusts to His people is to be held loosely and spent freely for His glory and the salvation of souls, as Haldane spent his all.
